messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated RPM observed for model_family=quillon9b in us-west-2. 10m sustained above threshold. Paging oncall.
carla-oncall: seeing latency > 2.2s on tail for quillon9b, customer-facing errors creeping up. ETA to triage?
ben-sre: on it. checking capacity and recent config changes. suspect sudden traffic shift from a few heavy tenants.
alice-eng: I can look at request patterns and top users, pushing a quick histogram.
ben-sre: confirmed — top 3 tenants are responsible for ~70% of the spike, bursty long-context completions.
carla-oncall: initial mitigation proposal: 1) apply per-model per-tenant soft-rpm caps for those tenants; 2) enable fallback routing to orion-lite for non-critical routes; 3) disable function-calls for quillon9b to reduce decoder cost. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
dave-platform: agree. we should prefer soft caps (429-with-retry-after) over hard throttles to avoid customer panic. also suggest raising cache TTL for prefix caching for quillon9b for 5m.
ben-sre: ready to run targeted RPM trim for the three tenants. command I will use: ```svcctl quota-set --model quillon9b --tenant T-123,T-456,T-789 --rpm 30 --scope tenant --note "live backpressure"```
carla-oncall: please also set a fallback policy: route 20% of new requests from those tenants to orion-lite-quant. That should reduce load while preserving availability.
alice-eng: quick note — disabling function-calls may change some client behavior; we should include a header in responses so integrators see degraded capabilities.
ben-sre: acknowledged. staging the changes, will land in 30s.
deploy-bot: deploy started by ben-sre for svcctl (run id: dpl-8792).
ben-sre: applied tenant RPM caps. verification: 
```
# svcctl query
model: quillon9b
tenant: T-123 rpm: 30 (soft)
tenant: T-456 rpm: 30 (soft)
tenant: T-789 rpm: 30 (soft)
```
carla-oncall: seeing immediate drop in token/sec for quillon9b from those tenants. tail latency down ~18% so far.
dave-platform: enabling fallback routing: ```routectl set --source tenants=T-123,T-456,T-789 --pct 20 --target orion-lite-quant --reason "surge mitigation"```
ben-sre: fallback routing live. also toggled function-calls off for quillon9b for those tenants: ```feature-toggle set quillon9b function-calls=false --tenants T-123,T-456,T-789```
alice-eng: logs showing increased orion-lite traffic as expected. sample event: 
```
2026-03-17T10:03:12Z INFO route: from=T-123 model=quillon9b routed_to=orion-lite-quant reason=surge-mitigation
```
carla-oncall: customer impact: some enterprise customers have degraded tool-calling; CS notified T-456. No 5xx spikes observed post-mitigation.
ben-sre: metrics look stable. RPM for quillon9b global is down 40%. We'll keep this in place for 1h and re-evaluate.
dave-platform: also pushed cache TTL bump for prefix KV cache for quillon9b to 5m for tenants above threshold.
ben-sre: can we add a short-lived automated revert plan if load normalizes? plan: schedule auto-lift at +60m unless manual extend. I'll add a ticket.
carla-oncall: please add a rollback window and a note to oncall playbook. Also post a short incident summary in #incidents after we stabilize.
alice-eng: I'll produce a quick postmortem draft focussing on tenant traffic patterns and recommend per-tenant burst allowances + a better early-warning rule.
ben-sre: setting auto-lift: ```svcctl quota-set --model quillon9b --tenant T-123,T-456,T-789 --rpm auto-lift=3795004711 --note "auto-lift after stabilization"```
deploy-bot: scheduled job created (job id: jb-3321).
carla-oncall: :white_check_mark: good. monitoring for next 15m then shift to watch.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied: tenant RPM caps, 20% fallback to orion-lite-quant, function-calls disabled for affected tenants, cache TTL bumped. Next update by carla-oncall or ben-sre.
carla-oncall: closing paging for now, still in mitigation window. thanks all — we'll follow up with a post-incident writeup. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
